# Proxima LLM Instructions

Proxima is a durable typed memory substrate for agentic systems. Use it through
MCP. Do not inspect or mutate the database directly.

## Discovery Order

1. Read `initialize.instructions` from the MCP server.
2. Call `tools/list`.
3. Call `resources/list` and `resources/templates/list`.
4. Read `proxima://how-to`.
5. Read `proxima://tools` for the live tool catalog.

Live server discovery is authoritative. This file is a compact offline guide.

## Hard Law

No tool writes a connection. An edge carries no information beyond its
existence, so every edge is a consequence of what some node says: an `origin`
entry from the handles a write declares it was made from, a `reference` entry
from a schema-declared payload field. Nothing you call takes an edge kind as an
argument.

To semantically relate Facts, derive an Abstraction over them with
`core_derive(kind="Abstraction", source_handles=[...])`; those handles land the
`origin` entries. When the claim is a judgment about memories that already
exist — a reason and a confidence — call `core_interpret`, which authors an
interpretation Perspective over its `subjects` and returns a `P:` handle; the
connections are that Perspective's own references. A Fact never interprets:
layering refuses a Fact as an interpretation source.

## Tool Choice

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| find prior knowledge | `core_search_memories` |
| record an observation | `core_remember` |
| capture a pattern/lesson | `core_derive` as `Abstraction` |
| record stance/self-model | `core_derive` as `Perspective` |
| claim what existing memories mean | `core_interpret` if advertised |
| set/refine objective | `core_goal` if advertised |
| relate/connect memories | no connect verb — derive or interpret over them |

## Edge Kinds

Two kinds, and the vocabulary is closed. The kind follows the write that
produced the row; nobody picks one.

| Kind | Written by | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| `origin` | the write that declares what it was made from (`source_handles` on `core_derive`) | new Abstraction/Perspective → each source memory |
| `reference` | a schema-declared payload field of the node itself | referrer → referent |

Writes that produce edges report an `edge_count`, not edge handles: a row is
`(source, target, kind, created_at)` and has no id to dereference.

Search before architectural/debugging work. Consolidate durable decisions and
gotchas at natural breaks. Use idempotency keys for replayable writes.

## Safety

- There is no dev or master-token bypass. All MCP auth is a host bearer
  (OIDC by default), including on loopback; retired `pxm_*` tokens fail
  closed. Local development runs a local issuer, not a weaker auth path.
- Non-loopback bind requires explicit exposure gates.
- Do not call tools not advertised by the current server profile.

## Write Discipline

- Facts are observations.
- Abstractions are operator-authored generalizations with provenance.
- Perspectives are stance/self-model rows.
- Goals are separate entities, not memories.
- Store durable why, not full transcripts.

## Useful Resources

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `proxima://how-to` | live usage guide generated by server profile |
| `proxima://tools` | live tool catalog |
| `proxima://memory/{id}` | memory details |
| `proxima://change-events{?since,limit}` | pull change events |
| `proxima://wake-candidates{?fact,limit}` | armed Goals woken by a trigger Fact |
| `proxima://edges{?kind,source,target,limit,cursor}` | list connections; at least one filter required |
